newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil - low sulphur busy, high sulphur slow.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil - low sulphur busy, high sulphur slow.

text.p: Low sulphur cracked fuel had a busy day on Thursday with two cargoes heard sold.
A 45-50,000 tonne low sulphur cracked cargo was rumoured to have been sold out of Scandinavia to a trader, but details on a price were not forthcoming.
"Its the best kept secret of the day," commented one trader at a major. "Its still unclear, some people think it went fixed, others that it was done at low quotes," said another.
A smaller 25-30,000 tonne cargo loading January 3-7 out of Denmark was done to a trader at $124 fob NWE.
Some saw the the load port as a touch difficult.
The low sulphur market has been under pressure this week although some dealers feel an upturn is around the corner in the New Year.
The high sulphur cracked market was unable to match the low sulphur sector. Material was available to meet limited demand.
"No one is taking positions, its just bits and bobs," said one trader who pegged prices steady around $115 cif.
High sulphur barges regained some lustre moving up to $119 fob ARA a tonne amid fairly good shipper demand.
